questions.question: Which attribute on a script element allows an inline or external script to execute only when its cryptographic nonce matches the page's Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header?

options.text: nonce
integrity
crossorigin
referrerpolicy

questions.explanation: The nonce attribute holds a single-use cryptographic token generated by the server per response; if it matches the CSP script-src 'nonce-...' directive, the browser permits script execution.

questions.question: What is the effect of setting type="module" on a script element in HTML?

options.text: It enables static ES module import and export statements inside the script.
It automatically defers script execution until after HTML parsing completes, even without a defer attribute.
It fetches external module scripts using CORS mode by default.
It executes the script in sloppy (non-strict) mode unless "use strict" is written.

questions.explanation: Module scripts (<script type="module">) support ES imports, are deferred automatically, enforce strict mode by default, and require valid CORS headers when loaded cross-origin.

questions.question: What does the nomodule boolean attribute on a classic script tag instruct modern browsers to do?

options.text: Skip downloading and executing the script if the browser supports ES modules.
Strip all import and export syntax before running the script.

questions.explanation: Browsers that understand <script type="module"> ignore scripts marked with nomodule, allowing developers to serve legacy polyfilled bundles exclusively to older browsers.

questions.question: Which HTML element provides fallback content that renders only when scripting is disabled in the user's browser or unsupported?

options.text: noscript
fallback
template
altscript

questions.explanation: The noscript element defines alternative HTML content displayed when JavaScript is turned off or blocked.
questions.code_snippet: Please enable JavaScript to use the interactive calculator.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a link element with rel="canonical" in the document head?

options.text: It tells search engines which URL is the authoritative master version when duplicate or parameterized URLs serve identical content.
It automatically redirects users from HTTP to HTTPS.
It defines the root base path for all relative image URLs on the page.
It locks the browser's address bar so query strings cannot be appended.

questions.explanation: A canonical link element consolidates indexing signals when the same page is reachable via multiple URLs (such as tracking parameters or pagination filters).

questions.question: In HTML5, the title element inside the head may contain formatting tags such as strong or em to style the browser tab text.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The title element has a text-only content model; any tags placed inside title are parsed literally as plain characters rather than HTML elements.

questions.question: Which global attribute makes an element's text directly editable by the user inside the browser?

options.text: contenteditable
editable
designmode
writable

questions.explanation: Setting contenteditable="true" (or "plaintext-only") turns any HTML element into a rich-text or plain-text editable region.
questions.code_snippet: Click here to edit this note directly.

questions.question: Which values are valid for the global dir attribute to control text directionality?

options.text: ltr (left-to-right)
rtl (right-to-left)
auto (browser determines direction from first strong directional character)
ttb (top-to-bottom)

questions.explanation: The dir attribute accepts ltr, rtl, or auto (essential for user-generated content in mixed scripts like Arabic, Hebrew, and English). Vertical writing modes are handled in CSS, not via dir.

questions.question: What is the semantic function of the bdi (Bidirectional Isolate) element?

options.text: It isolates a span of text whose directionality is unknown (such as a username) so it does not corrupt the bidirectional layout of surrounding punctuation or numbers.
It mirrors all characters horizontally like a reflection.
It forces right-to-left text to be read strictly from left to right.
It marks text that requires a right-to-left font file download.

questions.explanation: The bdi element isolates dynamic user-supplied strings inside sentences so an RTL username followed by a number or colon does not reorder adjacent LTR text.

questions.question: Which HTML element defines an import map in JSON format so bare module specifiers (like import 'lodash') resolve to URLs natively in the browser?

options.text: <script type="importmap">
<link rel="importmap">
<meta name="importmap">
<module-map>

questions.explanation: <script type="importmap"> contains a JSON object with an "imports" mapping that lets browsers resolve bare ES module names without a bundler.

questions.question: How do the rel="preload" and rel="prefetch" resource hints on a link tag differ in priority and intent?

options.text: preload fetches high-priority resources needed for the current page navigation, whereas prefetch speculatively fetches low-priority resources for likely future navigations.
preload works only for CSS stylesheets, whereas prefetch works only for JavaScript files.

questions.explanation: preload instructs the browser to download an asset critical to the current page immediately (requiring an as attribute), while prefetch downloads assets during idle time for the next page.

questions.question: Which attribute is required alongside rel="preload" on a link element so the browser can apply proper Content Security Policy checks and prioritization?

options.text: as
role
kind
fetch

questions.explanation: The as attribute (with values like "style", "script", "font", or "image") tells the browser the destination type of the preloaded resource so it sets accurate request headers and priorities.

questions.question: What does the popover global attribute enable when placed on an HTML element such as a div or menu?

options.text: It promotes the element to the top layer when triggered, supporting native light-dismiss on outside click or Escape key without custom z-index stacking hacks.
It opens the element in a separate OS browser popup window.
It turns any element into a draggable floating toolbar.
It displays the element's title attribute as a styled tooltip on hover.

questions.explanation: The HTML Popover API (popover="auto" or "manual", paired with popovertarget on a button) renders overlays in the browser's top layer with built-in light-dismiss and toggle behavior.

questions.question: Which URL scheme in an anchor element's href attribute triggers the user's default telephone dialer application on supported devices?

options.text: tel:
phone:
call:
sms://

questions.explanation: The tel: URI scheme (ideally formatted in international E.164 notation such as tel:+1-555-019-2834) invokes phone dialing on mobile and desktop VoIP clients.

questions.question: Which meta element configures the browser's UI chrome color (such as the mobile address bar or PWA title bar) to match a site's brand palette?

options.text: <meta name="theme-color" content="#1e293b">
<meta name="chrome-color" content="#1e293b">
<meta name="status-bar" content="#1e293b">
<link rel="theme" color="#1e293b">

questions.explanation: The theme-color meta tag suggests a CSS color value that supporting browsers use to tint surrounding browser UI elements.

questions.question: When using HTML entities, why must the ampersand character (&) be escaped as & inside href URLs that contain multiple query parameters?

options.text: To prevent the HTML parser from misinterpreting a query parameter name (like &copy=1 or &reg=true) as a named character reference.
Because HTTP servers reject URLs containing raw ampersand characters.
To URL-encode the ampersand as %26 before sending the GET request.
Because raw ampersands terminate the href attribute string early.

questions.explanation: If a query parameter matches a legacy HTML entity prefix (such as &copy or &para), an unescaped ampersand can be decoded into a symbol instead of remaining a literal parameter separator.

questions.question: In HTML5, an element's id attribute value is allowed to start with a numeric digit (for example, id="1st-section").

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Unlike HTML4, HTML5 permits any non-empty string without ASCII whitespace as a valid id value, including leading digits (though CSS selectors require escaping leading digits).

questions.question: Which attributes on an anchor element can communicate metadata about the linked resource without altering navigation behavior?

options.text: hreflang (indicates the language of the linked document)
type (hints at the MIME type of the linked resource)
rel (describes the relationship between the current document and the linked URL)
charset (overrides the server's UTF-8 encoding header)

questions.explanation: hreflang, type, and rel are standard advisory attributes on anchor tags. The charset attribute on anchor elements is obsolete in HTML5.

questions.question: What does the draggable="true" attribute do on a standard HTML element such as a div or li?

options.text: It enables native HTML Drag and Drop API events (dragstart, drag, dragend) on that element.
It automatically moves the element's DOM position when dragged and dropped anywhere on the page.
It converts the element into a resizable modal window.
It disables text selection inside all child elements.

questions.explanation: By default, only images, links, and text selections are draggable. Setting draggable="true" opts any element into the HTML Drag and Drop event lifecycle, though JavaScript must handle drop placement.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the blocking="render" attribute on a script or link rel="stylesheet" element?

options.text: It explicitly instructs the browser to hold first paint until that critical script or stylesheet has finished loading and executing.
It prevents the browser from ever rendering the linked stylesheet.
It forces async scripts to execute before DOMContentLoaded.
It blocks third-party tracking pixels inside the document body.

questions.explanation: The blocking="render" attribute prevents flashes of unstyled or unhydrated content by keeping the document render-blocked until an essential script (such as a critical theme loader) completes.

questions.question: What is the semantic difference between the em element and the i element?

options.text: em indicates stress emphasis that changes the meaning of a sentence, while i marks an alternate voice, technical term, taxonomic name, or ship name.
em is a block-level element, while i is an inline element.

questions.explanation: Both render in italics by default, but em expresses verbal stress emphasis (which screen readers may inflect), whereas i denotes idiomatic phrases, foreign words, or taxonomic names.
questions.code_snippet: I never said she stole the money. The specimen is Panthera leo.

questions.question: When marking up an abbreviation with the abbr element, which attribute is conventionally used to provide the full expansion of the acronym?

options.text: title
alt
expansion
full

questions.explanation: The global title attribute on an abbr element holds the unabbreviated expansion (e.g., <abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr>).
questions.code_snippet: We follow WCAG 2.2 standards.

questions.question: What does the dfn element represent when placed around a term inside a paragraph or description list?

options.text: The defining instance of a term whose definition is provided in the nearest ancestor paragraph, description list item, or section.
A footnote reference number at the end of a sentence.
A deprecated function name in API documentation.
A default fallback value inside a template.

questions.explanation: The dfn element marks the specific occurrence where a term is formally defined in the surrounding text.
questions.code_snippet: Idempotence is the property of certain operations whereby they can be applied multiple times without changing the result beyond the initial application.

questions.question: Which HTML element represents the small print of a document, such as copyright notices, legal disclaimers, or licensing terms?

options.text: small
sub
aside
footer

questions.explanation: In HTML5, small was redefined from a purely presentational font-size tag into a semantic element for side comments, disclaimers, and copyright text.

questions.question: What is the semantic meaning of the ins element in HTML5?

options.text: A range of text that has been added to a document as part of a tracked revision.
Any text that should be styled with a decorative underline.
An inline input field embedded inside a paragraph.
An instructional callout box for new users.

questions.explanation: Paired with del, the ins element marks editorial additions to a document and supports optional cite and datetime attributes.

questions.question: Which HTML element is semantically appropriate for marking up a toolbar or list of interactive commands/actions?

options.text: menu
nav
dl
command

questions.explanation: In modern HTML, menu is a semantic alternative to ul specifically intended for an unordered list of interactive buttons or commands (such as a rich-text editor toolbar).

questions.question: In HTML5, using the u element simply to underline non-link text for visual emphasis is discouraged because users confuse underlines with hyperlinks; instead, u is reserved for unarticulated annotations like misspelled words.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: HTML5 defines u for spans of text with an unarticulated, non-textual annotation—such as flagging spelling errors or proper-name marks in Chinese text—rather than general decoration.
questions.code_snippet: Check the spelling of recieve.

questions.question: How do the sub and sup elements differ in usage?

options.text: sub renders subscript text below the baseline (e.g., H2O), while sup renders superscript text above the baseline (e.g., E=mc2).
sub represents a subtitle below a heading, while sup represents a super-heading above h1.

questions.explanation: sub and sup represent typographical subscript and superscript notations where baseline positioning carries specific meaning in chemical formulas, exponents, or ordinal numbers.
questions.code_snippet: Water is H2O, and area is measured in m2.

questions.question: Which HTML element is designed to display East Asian ruby annotations (phonetic pronunciation guides like furigana) alongside base characters?

options.text: ruby
rt
rp
rbc

questions.explanation: Ruby annotations use ruby as the wrapper, rt for the ruby text pronunciation, and rp for fallback parentheses in browsers that do not render ruby layout.

questions.question: What is the semantic role of the data element in HTML5?

options.text: It links human-readable content with a machine-readable translation in its value attribute (such as a product SKU or numeric sort key).
It embeds an inline JSON database inside the document body.
It replaces td cells inside data-heavy financial tables.
It defines custom data-* attributes globally for the document.

questions.explanation: Similar to how time uses datetime for dates, the data element pairs human-friendly text with a machine-readable value attribute (such as an inventory ID or raw numeric price).

questions.question: When marking up a multi-line block of computer source code, why is code conventionally nested inside a pre element?

options.text: Because code alone is an inline element that collapses whitespace, whereas pre preserves exact newlines and indentation.
Because HTML syntax forbids using code without a parent pre element.
Because pre automatically applies syntax highlighting colors based on the class attribute.
Because code inside pre disables HTML entity escaping for < and > characters.

questions.explanation: The pre element preserves whitespace and line breaks in a monospace font, while the nested code element supplies the semantic meaning that the preformatted text is computer code.

questions.question: What does the hr element semantically represent in HTML5?

options.text: A thematic break between paragraph-level elements, such as a scene change in a story or a transition to another topic within a section.
A purely decorative horizontal border line beneath headings.
A mandatory page break when printing the HTML document.
The boundary separating head and body sections.

questions.explanation: In HTML5, hr represents a thematic break in narrative or topical flow (not merely a visual rule; decorative borders should use CSS border).

questions.question: Which HTML element should wrap a group of heading and subheading elements (such as an h1 and a subtitle p) so they are treated as a single logical heading unit?

options.text: hgroup
header
titlegroup
caption

questions.explanation: In the HTML Living Standard, hgroup groups a single h1–h6 heading with one or more secondary p elements (such as a tagline, kicker, or subtitle).

questions.question: When is the aside element semantically appropriate?

options.text: For a pull quote or glossary sidebar tangentially related to the surrounding article.
For a site-wide sidebar containing related posts, advertising, or secondary navigation.
For the primary content of a blog post.
For inline parenthetical remarks inside a single sentence.

questions.explanation: aside represents a section of a page whose content is tangentially related to the content around it and could be considered separate from that main flow.

questions.question: Can multiple details elements share the same name attribute to create an exclusive accordion where opening one automatically closes the others?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Modern HTML supports the name attribute on details elements; grouping multiple details tags with the same name creates a native exclusive accordion without JavaScript.

questions.question: What is the semantic difference between ol and ul elements?

options.text: ol represents a list where changing the sequence of items alters the meaning (such as recipe steps or rankings), whereas ul represents a collection where order is non-critical.
ol can only contain text strings, whereas ul can contain nested lists and links.

questions.explanation: Both ol and ul accept identical child li elements (which can contain nested lists or block content); the choice depends strictly on whether item ordering carries semantic significance.

questions.question: Which attributes on an ol element allow customizing the numbering sequence directly in HTML without CSS counters?

options.text: start (sets the starting integer for the list)
reversed (numbers the list items in descending order)
type (selects numbering marker kind such as 1, a, A, i, I)
step (increments list numbers by a custom interval)

questions.explanation: Ordered lists natively support start, reversed, and type (as well as value on individual li elements), whereas step is only valid on form inputs.

questions.question: In HTML5, is it valid to wrap a dt and dd pair inside a div element within a dl description list?

options.text: Yes, HTML explicitly allows div elements as direct children of dl to group term-description pairs for styling or microdata.
No, only dt and dd elements are ever permitted inside a dl element.
Yes, but only if the div has role="listitem".
No, wrapping dt/dd requires using a section element instead of div.

questions.explanation: The HTML specification explicitly permits div children inside dl solely to wrap groups of dt and dd elements (for example, to style each key-value pair as a CSS grid row).

questions.question: When a dialog element is closed using dialog.close('confirm'), where is the passed string argument stored on the DOM element?

options.text: dialog.returnValue
dialog.value
dialog.result
dialog.dataset.return

questions.explanation: The native HTMLDialogElement exposes a returnValue property that captures either the argument passed to close() or the value of the submit button when a <form method="dialog"> closes the modal.
questions.code_snippet: Delete this file?

questions.question: What happens when a button inside a <form method="dialog"> is clicked while inside an open dialog element?

options.text: It closes the dialog without making an HTTP network request and sets dialog.returnValue to the clicked button's value attribute.
It sends an HTTP GET request to the current page URL with query parameters.
It throws a NotSupportedError because forms cannot use method="dialog".
It resets all inputs inside the dialog without closing it.

questions.explanation: method="dialog" is a built-in HTML form method designed specifically for dialog elements: submitting it closes the dialog and fires a close event with the button's returnValue.

questions.question: What is the difference between <input type="datetime-local"> and <input type="date">?

options.text: datetime-local captures both a calendar date and wall-clock time (without timezone offset), whereas date captures only year, month, and day.
datetime-local automatically converts user input into UTC ISO strings with a Z suffix, whereas date submits localized month names.

questions.explanation: datetime-local submits values formatted as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM without timezone data, while date submits YYYY-MM-DD.

questions.question: Which HTML5 input type renders a slider control for selecting a numeric value within a min and max range?

options.text: type="range"
type="slider"
type="meter"
type="scale"

questions.explanation: <input type="range"> renders a native slider widget defaulting to min="0" and max="100" when omitted.
questions.code_snippet:
<label for="vol">Volume</label>
<input id="vol" type="range" name="volume" min="0" max="100" step="5">

questions.question: How do the minlength and maxlength attributes work together on text inputs and textareas?

options.text: maxlength prevents users from typing or pasting beyond the character limit, while minlength triggers constraint validation only if the user enters non-empty text shorter than the minimum.
minlength automatically makes the field required even if the required attribute is omitted.
Both attributes count UTF-8 byte length rather than UTF-16 code units.
maxlength truncates form submission silently on the server without notifying the user.

questions.explanation: If a field is optional (no required attribute) and left completely blank, minlength passes validation; it only fails if the user enters 1 to (minlength - 1) characters.

questions.question: Which attribute on a select element allows the user to select more than one option at the same time?

options.text: multiple
multiselect
size="many"
array

questions.explanation: The boolean multiple attribute turns a select dropdown into a scrollable multi-select list box that submits one key-value pair per selected option.
questions.code_snippet:
<select name="skills" multiple size="4">
  <option value="html">HTML</option>
  <option value="css">CSS</option>
  <option value="js">JavaScript</option>
</select>

questions.question: What happens when a fieldset element has the boolean disabled attribute applied to it?

options.text: All descendant form controls inside the fieldset are disabled, except any form controls located inside its first child legend element.
Only the fieldset border turns gray while inner inputs remain editable.
Every control including inputs inside the first legend element is disabled.
The fieldset and all its children are hidden from the page.

questions.explanation: Disabling a fieldset disables all nested inputs, selects, and buttons in bulk—while intentionally keeping controls inside the first legend active (useful for a checkbox in the legend that enables/disables the section).
questions.code_snippet:
<fieldset disabled>
  <legend><label><input type="checkbox"> Enable Custom Billing</label></legend>
  <input type="text" name="vat_id" placeholder="VAT Number">
</fieldset>

questions.question: Which attributes are valid on an <input type="file"> element?

options.text: multiple (allows selecting multiple files)
accept (specifies allowed MIME types or file extensions)
capture (hints mobile browsers to open the camera or microphone directly)
maxsize (restricts upload size in bytes)

questions.explanation: File inputs support multiple, accept, and capture ("user" or "environment"). There is no HTML attribute to enforce maximum file size; that requires JavaScript File.size checks and server limits.

questions.question: What value format does <input type="color"> expect in its value attribute and submit when a form is sent?

options.text: A 7-character lowercase hexadecimal string such as #ff5733.
An RGB functional notation string such as rgb(255, 87, 51).
A 3-character shorthand hex string such as #f53.
A CSS named color keyword such as coral.

questions.explanation: The HTML color input strictly uses 6-digit hexadecimal sRGB notation prefixed with # (e.g., #000000); shorthand hex, rgb(), and color names are invalid.

questions.question: In HTML5, setting a custom attribute name="_charset_" on an <input type="hidden"> causes the browser to automatically populate its value with the character encoding used to submit the form.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Per the HTML form submission algorithm, an <input type="hidden" name="_charset_"> without a value attribute is automatically filled with the submission character encoding (such as UTF-8).

questions.question: Why should a placeholder attribute never be used as a replacement for a visible label element?

options.text: Placeholder text disappears as soon as the user starts typing, hurting short-term memory and error review.
Placeholder text often has low color contrast by default and is not a reliable accessible name across all assistive technologies.
Clicking a placeholder does not provide a larger hit area outside the input box like a label does.
HTML5 validators throw a fatal syntax error when placeholder is used without label.

questions.explanation: Placeholders are meant for short format hints (e.g., 'e.g., 555-0199'), not field labels, because vanishing text creates usability, cognitive, and accessibility barriers.

questions.question: What does the dirname attribute on a text input or textarea submit alongside the field's value?

options.text: An additional form field containing the resolved text direction ("ltr" or "rtl") of the user's input.
The local directory path of an uploaded file.
The domain name of the referring web page.
The horizontal scroll offset of the text box.

questions.explanation: When <input name="comment" dirname="comment.dir"> is submitted, the browser sends both comment=... and comment.dir=ltr (or rtl) so servers preserve text directionality.

questions.question: Which enterkeyhint attribute value changes the mobile virtual keyboard's action key label to indicate sending a message or submitting a chat input?

options.text: enterkeyhint="send"
enterkeyhint="submit"
enterkeyhint="chat"
enterkeyhint="post"

questions.explanation: The global enterkeyhint attribute accepts enter, done, go, next, previous, search, and send to tailor the Enter key icon/label on virtual keyboards.

questions.question: What is the behavior of an <input type="reset"> button inside a form?

options.text: It restores all form controls to their initial HTML default values (such as the value attribute or checked state), not necessarily clearing them to blank.
It wipes every input in the form to an empty string and clears all server session cookies.

questions.explanation: Resetting a form reverts controls back to their initial DOM defaultValue / defaultChecked states specified in the markup.

questions.question: Which autocomplete token is standardized for one-time SMS or authenticator verification codes so mobile browsers can auto-suggest incoming OTP codes?

options.text: autocomplete="one-time-code"
autocomplete="otp"
autocomplete="2fa-code"
autocomplete="sms-token"

questions.explanation: autocomplete="one-time-code" lets mobile operating systems detect incoming SMS verification codes and offer one-tap autofill above the keyboard.
questions.code_snippet:
<label for="otp">Verification Code</label>
<input id="otp" type="text" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="one-time-code">

questions.question: How does <input type="tel"> differ from <input type="email"> in HTML5 browser validation?

options.text: type="tel" performs no automatic format validation because international phone formats vary widely, whereas type="email" validates email syntax.
type="tel" restricts input strictly to digits 0-9 and blocks plus signs or hyphens.
type="tel" automatically formats numbers with parentheses as the user types.
type="tel" is only supported on mobile phones and falls back to type="number" on desktop.

questions.explanation: Because global phone numbering conventions differ greatly, browsers trigger a telephone keypad for type="tel" without enforcing a built-in regex unless you add a pattern attribute.

questions.question: Which attribute on a form element specifies the character encodings the server accepts for form submission?

options.text: accept-charset
charset
encoding
content-encoding

questions.explanation: The accept-charset attribute on a form element specifies allowed character encodings (in HTML5, the only conforming value is "UTF-8").

questions.question: Which form elements are considered 'labelable' elements that can be associated with a label element via for/id?

options.text: input (except type="hidden")
select and textarea
meter and progress
fieldset

questions.explanation: Labelable elements in HTML include button, input (not hidden), meter, output, progress, select, and textarea. A fieldset is labeled by a legend, not a label element.

questions.question: What happens when a user presses Enter while focused inside a single-line <input type="text"> inside a form that contains a submit button?

options.text: The browser triggers implicit form submission using the form's default (first) submit button.
The browser inserts a newline character inside the text input.
Focus moves to the next input field without submitting.
Nothing happens unless a keydown event listener is manually attached.

questions.explanation: HTML specifies implicit submission when Enter is pressed inside an active single-line text-like input, activating the form's first submit button in tree order.

questions.question: What is the role of the spellcheck global attribute when placed on an input or textarea?

options.text: It hints whether the browser should check the element's text for spelling and grammar errors ("true" or "false").
It blocks form submission if any misspelled words are detected.
It automatically replaces misspelled words without user confirmation.
It downloads a custom dictionary file specified in the lang attribute.

questions.explanation: Setting spellcheck="false" is particularly helpful on inputs for usernames, code snippets, or tracking numbers so red squiggly underlines do not clutter non-prose text.

questions.question: When an <input type="image" src="go.png" alt="Search"> is clicked to submit a form, what extra parameters does the browser include in the submission?

options.text: The X and Y click coordinates relative to the image as x and y (or name.x and name.y).
The base64-encoded binary data of the button image.
The alt text string as the form's primary action parameter.
The natural width and height of the image in pixels.

questions.explanation: An image submit button sends the pixel coordinates where the user clicked (x and y, or name.x and name.y if named).

questions.question: Which attribute on a button or input type="submit" prevents the browser from running HTML5 constraint validation only when that specific button is clicked?

options.text: formnovalidate
novalidate
skipvalidate
disabled

questions.explanation: novalidate goes on the <form> tag itself, whereas formnovalidate goes on an individual submit button so other submit buttons in the same form still validate.

questions.question: How do tabindex="0" and tabindex="-1" differ when applied to a non-interactive element like a div or section?

options.text: tabindex="0" inserts the element into the natural keyboard Tab order, whereas tabindex="-1" excludes it from Tab navigation while still allowing programmatic focus via element.focus().
tabindex="0" hides the element from screen readers, whereas tabindex="-1" announces it first on page load.

questions.explanation: tabindex="-1" is ideal for target headings or modal containers that should receive programmatic focus when opened without cluttering the user's Tab sequence.

questions.question: When building a custom toggle button (such as a 'Mute' or 'Favorite' button whose label stays constant while its active state toggles), which ARIA attribute communicates its pressed state?

options.text: aria-pressed="true" or "false"
aria-expanded="true" or "false"
aria-current="true" or "false"
aria-active="true" or "false"

questions.explanation: aria-pressed turns a standard button into a toggle button in the accessibility tree (supporting "true", "false", and "mixed").

questions.question: Which ARIA attributes are required on a custom progress bar or slider widget built with role="progressbar" or role="slider"?

options.text: aria-valuenow
aria-valuemin
aria-valuemax
aria-step

questions.explanation: Range widgets like role="slider" and determinate role="progressbar" require aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, and aria-valuenow (plus optional aria-valuetext for human-friendly units). aria-step does not exist.

questions.question: What does the aria-atomic="true" attribute do when paired with an aria-live region?

options.text: It instructs assistive technologies to announce the entire live region as a whole even if only a single child text node changed.
It prevents multiple updates from firing within the same millisecond.
It restricts screen reader announcements to only the individual changed character.
It automatically focuses the live region whenever its content updates.

questions.explanation: When updating a status message like 'Page 2 of 10', setting aria-atomic="true" ensures the screen reader reads 'Page 2 of 10' instead of just '2'.

questions.question: An HTML section element without an accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby) is automatically exposed as a navigation landmark in screen reader landmark lists.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: A section element only maps to the ARIA region landmark role when it has an explicit accessible name via aria-label or aria-labelledby; otherwise, it has a generic role.

questions.question: When an inline SVG is purely decorative inside a button that already has visible text, how should the SVG be marked up for accessibility?

options.text: Add aria-hidden="true" (and focusable="false" for legacy IE/Edge compatibility) on the svg element.
Add alt="icon" directly onto the svg element.
Add role="img" and aria-label="icon" onto the svg element.
Wrap the svg inside a figcaption element.

questions.explanation: When adjacent text already describes the button's action, hiding the decorative icon with aria-hidden="true" prevents redundant screen reader announcements.
questions.code_snippet:
<button type="submit">
  <svg aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" width="16" height="16">...</svg>
  Download Report
</button>

questions.question: Conversely, when a standalone inline SVG conveys meaningful content (such as a company logo or chart) without adjacent text, how do you give it an accessible name?

options.text: Add role="img" on the svg element along with aria-label or a child <title> element referenced via aria-labelledby.
Add an alt attribute directly on the svg tag.
Add a placeholder attribute on the svg tag.
Set aria-hidden="false" without any label attributes.

questions.explanation: Unlike ,
questions.code_snippet:
<svg role="img" aria-labelledby="logo-title" viewBox="0 0 120 40">
  <title id="logo-title">Acme Cloud Logo</title>
  ...
</svg>

questions.question: Which ARIA role and attributes are used to construct an accessible tabbed interface?

options.text: role="tablist" on the container holding the tab buttons
role="tab" and aria-selected="true"/"false" on each tab button
role="tabpanel" on each content panel
role="accordion" on the outer wrapper

questions.explanation: The WAI-ARIA Tabs pattern pairs role="tablist", role="tab" (with aria-selected and aria-controls), and role="tabpanel" (with aria-labelledby). role="accordion" does not exist in ARIA.
questions.code_snippet: ...

questions.question: Why is opening links automatically in a new tab (target="_blank") without warning considered poor accessibility practice unless clearly indicated?

options.text: It disorients screen reader and cognitive-disability users and breaks the browser's Back button history in the new tab.
Screen readers are unable to read any content inside a newly opened browser tab.
target="_blank" disables keyboard Tab navigation on the destination page.
Assistive technologies block all links containing a target attribute.

questions.explanation: Unexpected context changes violate WCAG Success Criterion 3.2.5; when target="_blank" is necessary, link text or visually hidden text should inform users that it opens in a new tab.
questions.code_snippet: Terms of Service (opens in a new tab)

questions.question: What does the aria-haspopup="menu" (or "dialog" / "listbox") attribute communicate on a trigger button?

options.text: It informs assistive technologies that activating the button opens an interactive popup widget of the specified type.
It causes the browser to render a native right-click context menu automatically.
It displays a browser title tooltip immediately on focus.
It forces the target element to open inside a new browser window.

questions.explanation: aria-haspopup indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element (menu, listbox, tree, grid, or dialog) triggered by a control.

questions.question: Which combination of attributes properly marks a required form input for both native HTML validation and assistive technologies?

options.text: Using the native HTML required attribute (which automatically exposes aria-required="true" in modern browsers) alongside a visible required indicator in the label.
Using only a red asterisk span with aria-hidden="true" and omitting both required and aria-required.

questions.explanation: Native required provides built-in validation and sets the accessibility tree's required state automatically, while a visible indicator in the label helps sighted users.

questions.question: What is the purpose of aria-busy="true" on a container element such as a feed or table?

options.text: It signals assistive technologies that the region is currently being updated asynchronously and to wait until aria-busy="false" before announcing changes.
It displays a native browser spinning loading cursor over the element.
It pauses JavaScript event loop execution inside that DOM subtree.
It disables all form inputs inside the container.

questions.explanation: Setting aria-busy="true" during multi-step DOM mutations prevents screen readers from announcing partial or incomplete intermediate states until loading finishes.

questions.question: When linking to an external stylesheet or font, why can placing multiple identical h1 elements across unrelated widgets on a page hinder accessibility?

options.text: It flattens the document outline so screen reader users cannot quickly locate the primary page title using the '1' heading shortcut.
HTML5 parsers strip any h1 element after the first occurrence.
Browsers render subsequent h1 elements at the same size as body paragraphs.
Screen readers refuse to read text inside a second h1 tag.

questions.explanation: Using a single main h1 for the page's primary topic followed by logical h2/h3 subheadings gives assistive technology users a clear structural landmark for the page title.

questions.question: What does role="alert" implicitly set on an element in ARIA?

options.text: Implicit aria-live="assertive" and aria-atomic="true" so urgent error messages are announced immediately.
Implicit aria-live="polite" and aria-hidden="true".
Implicit tabindex="0" and automatic focus theft.
Implicit role="dialog" with a modal backdrop.

questions.explanation: role="alert" is a live-region role with implicit assertive politeness and atomic announcement, designed for time-sensitive error notifications without moving keyboard focus.
questions.code_snippet: Payment declined. Please check your card number.

questions.question: Which HTML elements have an implicit ARIA role of 'generic' (meaning they convey no landmark or semantic structure on their own)?

options.text: div
span
main
article

questions.explanation: div and span are pure grouping/phrasing containers with no semantic role, whereas main maps to role="main" and article maps to role="article".

questions.question: In ARIA, a 'roving tabindex' pattern keeps tabindex="0" on only the currently active item inside a composite widget (like a toolbar or tablist) while setting tabindex="-1" on all sibling items.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Roving tabindex lets users enter a composite widget with a single Tab press, navigate internally using Arrow keys (which move tabindex="0" to the focused item), and exit with the next Tab press.

questions.question: When using aria-errormessage on an invalid input field, which companion attribute must also be set to "true" for assistive technologies to expose the error message?

options.text: aria-invalid="true"
aria-required="true"
aria-live="true"
aria-expanded="true"

questions.explanation: Per the WAI-ARIA specification, user agents only expose aria-errormessage when aria-invalid is set to "true" (or a validation token like "grammar"/"spelling").
questions.code_snippet: Please enter a valid email address.

questions.question: Why should you avoid placing interactive elements (such as a button or link) inside a heading tag (h1–h6) when the heading wraps a large card block?

options.text: Putting only the concise title text inside the link within the heading keeps the link's accessible name short and readable rather than reading an entire card's text.
HTML5 forbids placing an anchor tag inside an h2 or h3 element.
Links inside heading elements cannot be focused using the Tab key.
Screen readers ignore headings that contain child anchor elements.

questions.explanation: Anchors are allowed inside headings, and keeping only the title text inside the heading link ensures screen reader link lists remain clean and concise.
questions.code_snippet:
Mastering CSS Grid

A complete guide to two-dimensional layouts.

questions.question: What is the implicit ARIA landmark role of a header element when it is a direct child of body versus when it is nested inside an article or section?

options.text: It maps to role="banner" when scoped to the page body, but has no landmark role (generic) when nested inside article, aside, main, nav, or section.
It maps to role="banner" in every location across the document.
It maps to role="navigation" when inside body and role="banner" when inside article.
It never exposes any ARIA role unless role="banner" is added manually.

questions.explanation: Similarly, footer maps to role="contentinfo" only when scoped to the page body, preventing inner card headers/footers from polluting the page's landmark list.

questions.question: Which attribute on an html or section element allows screen readers to switch speech synthesis voice and pronunciation rules mid-page for a foreign-language quote?

options.text: lang
hreflang
srclang
translate

questions.explanation: The global lang attribute can be applied to any inline or block element (e.g., <blockquote lang="fr">) so assistive technologies pronounce foreign passages accurately.
questions.code_snippet: As the French say, c'est la vie.

questions.question: Which attribute allows a table cell (td or th) to span vertically down across four rows?

options.text: rowspan="4"
colspan="4"
height="4"
rows="4"

questions.explanation: rowspan="4" merges a cell downward across four table rows, reducing the number of cells needed in the subsequent three tr rows.

questions.question: What does the scope="rowgroup" attribute on a th element signify in a data table?

options.text: The header cell applies to all cells within its enclosing tbody, thead, or tfoot row group.
The header cell applies to a single horizontal tr row only.
The header cell collapses all rows inside its tbody when clicked.
The header cell applies to all columns defined inside a colgroup.

questions.explanation: When a table uses multiple tbody sections for grouped categories, a spanning th with scope="rowgroup" associates that category header with every row in that tbody.

questions.question: In an img element's srcset attribute, what does an x-descriptor like icon-2x.png 2x tell the browser?

options.text: Select this image candidate on displays with a device pixel ratio (DPR) of 2x (such as Retina/HiDPI screens).
Scale the image to twice the width of its parent container.
Download the image twice to verify network checksums.
Display the image at 200% zoom when hovered.

questions.explanation: Pixel density descriptors (1x, 2x, 3x) are used for fixed-width images to serve sharper assets on high-DPI screens without needing a sizes attribute.

questions.question: Inside a picture element, the order of child source elements matters because the browser selects the first source whose media and type conditions match.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: The browser evaluates source children from top to bottom and stops at the first matching source, so modern formats like AVIF must be listed before WebP, followed by the fallback img.

questions.question: How do the crossorigin="anonymous" and crossorigin="use-credentials" attributes behave on img, video, or audio elements?

options.text: anonymous sends a CORS Origin header without cookies/credentials, whereas use-credentials includes cookies and requires an explicit non-wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.
anonymous blocks cross-origin images completely, whereas use-credentials bypasses browser CORS restrictions.

questions.explanation: Setting crossorigin on media elements is essential when drawing cross-origin images onto an HTML canvas (to avoid tainting the canvas) or loading cross-origin WebVTT track files.

questions.question: Which attribute on a video element prevents mobile browsers (such as iOS Safari) from forcing the video into fullscreen playback as soon as it starts playing?

options.text: playsinline
nofullscreen
embedded
inline

questions.explanation: The boolean playsinline attribute instructs mobile browsers to play the video directly within its inline layout box rather than launching the native fullscreen media player.

questions.question: Which kind attribute values are valid on a WebVTT track element inside a video player?

options.text: captions (dialogue plus sound effects for deaf/hard-of-hearing viewers)
subtitles (translated dialogue for viewers who can hear the audio)
descriptions (textual descriptions of visual scenes for blind viewers)
transcript (full static essay rendered below the player)

questions.explanation: The HTML track element supports five kind values: subtitles, captions, descriptions, chapters, and metadata. transcript is not a valid track kind.

questions.question: Which attribute on a video or audio element lets you selectively hide native browser UI controls like the download button, fullscreen button, or remote playback?

options.text: controlslist (e.g., controlslist="nodownload nofullscreen")
hidecontrols="download"
sandbox="nodownload"
disablecontrols="true"

questions.explanation: The controlslist attribute accepts space-separated tokens such as nodownload, nofullscreen, and noremoteplayback to customize the native media control bar.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the srcdoc attribute on an iframe element?

options.text: It embeds inline HTML markup directly as the content of the iframe without needing an external URL, taking precedence over src if both are present.
It links to an external documentation PDF describing the iframe's API.
It displays fallback HTML only when the external src URL returns a 404 error.
It encodes the iframe's contents as a downloadable .html file.

questions.explanation: srcdoc allows rendering self-contained HTML strings (such as sandboxed email previews or live code playgrounds) inside an iframe without extra network requests.

questions.question: How does the allow attribute on an iframe control access to sensitive browser features like geolocation, camera, microphone, or fullscreen?

options.text: It defines a Permissions Policy delegating specific features (such as allow="fullscreen; camera 'self'") to the embedded origin.
It lists allowed MIME types that the iframe can download.
It replaces the sandbox attribute by granting full top-level navigation rights.
It specifies which CSS properties can inherit across the iframe boundary.

questions.explanation: The allow attribute enforces Permissions Policy rules on cross-origin iframes, blocking powerful APIs like camera, microphone, payment, and fullscreen unless explicitly delegated.
questions.code_snippet: <iframe src="https://video.example.com/embed/123" title="Video player" allow="autoplay; fullscreen; picture-in-picture"></iframe>

questions.question: What happens if an HTML canvas element is resized using CSS width and height properties without updating its HTML width and height attributes?

options.text: The underlying bitmap stays at the default 300x150 pixel resolution and stretches to fit the CSS box, resulting in blurry or distorted graphics.
The browser automatically reallocates the drawing buffer to match the CSS pixel size.
The canvas clears its drawing context and throws an IndexSizeError.
CSS width and height rules are completely ignored on canvas elements.

questions.explanation: A canvas has both an intrinsic coordinate buffer size (controlled by its HTML width/height attributes, defaulting to 300x150) and a CSS layout size; mismatched ratios stretch the raster bitmap.

questions.question: What is the purpose of fallback content placed between opening <canvas> and closing </canvas> tags?

options.text: It is exposed in the accessibility tree for screen readers and displayed in browsers where canvas is unsupported or disabled.
It renders automatically as a caption underneath the canvas drawing.
It is drawn onto the canvas as default placeholder text.
HTML syntax forbids placing any child nodes inside a canvas element.

questions.explanation: Unlike void elements, canvas has a closing tag and exposes its inner DOM fallback tree (such as an accessible data table or description) to assistive technologies.
questions.code_snippet: Bar chart showing Q1 revenue of $1.2M and Q2 revenue of $1.5M.

questions.question: Which HTML element provides a general-purpose container for external resources such as PDFs, SVG documents, or nested browsing contexts, supporting inner fallback markup?

options.text: object (using data and type attributes)
embed (which is a void element without fallback children)
source
frame

questions.explanation: The object element embeds external resources via data and type attributes and renders its inner child markup if the resource cannot be displayed, whereas embed is a void element.

questions.question: Why should HTML table elements never be used to construct multi-column page layouts?

options.text: Screen readers announce row and column counts and cell coordinates for non-tabular content unless role="presentation" is added.
Rigid row/column DOM structures prevent responsive reflowing across mobile and desktop viewports.
It mixes visual presentation into HTML markup instead of using CSS Grid or Flexbox.
Browsers refuse to render images or forms inside table cells.

questions.explanation: Tables are strictly for two-dimensional tabular data; layout tables harm accessibility navigation, break responsive adaptation, and bloat markup.

questions.question: In a colgroup element that contains child col elements, placing a span attribute on the colgroup tag itself is valid.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: According to the HTML specification, the span attribute is permitted on colgroup only when it has no child col elements; if child col tags are present, span must be placed on the col elements instead.

questions.question: Which attribute on an area element inside an image map specifies the geometric shape of the clickable hotspot?

options.text: shape (accepting rect, circle, poly, or default)
type (accepting box, round, or polygon)
region (accepting square, oval, or path)
clip (accepting inset, circle, or polygon)

questions.explanation: The area element uses shape="rect|circle|poly|default" paired with comma-separated pixel coordinates in coords.

questions.question: How do the loop and muted boolean attributes work on an HTML audio or video element?

options.text: loop automatically restarts playback from the beginning upon reaching the end, and muted initializes the audio output silenced.
loop repeats the media exactly three times, and muted permanently strips the audio track from the file.

questions.explanation: Both loop and muted are standard boolean attributes on HTMLMediaElement that control continuous repetition and initial audio silencing.

questions.question: When using a picture element for art direction (displaying a tightly cropped portrait image on mobile and a wide landscape image on desktop), which attribute on source specifies the viewport breakpoint?

options.text: media (accepting a valid CSS media query such as media="(max-width: 767px)")
sizes (accepting a media condition)
breakpoint (accepting a pixel integer)
viewport (accepting mobile or desktop)

questions.explanation: The media attribute on <source> inside <picture> evaluates CSS media queries so developers can serve completely different aspect ratios or crops per device class.

questions.question: Why is it important to provide an explicit sizes attribute whenever an img element uses width descriptors (w) in srcset?

options.text: Because the browser's preload scanner fetches images before CSS is parsed, so without sizes it assumes the image occupies 100vw and may download an overly large file.
Because browsers ignore the entire srcset attribute unless sizes is also present.
Because sizes sets the intrinsic pixel height of the downloaded image.
Because sizes compresses the image on the client side to fit the container.

questions.explanation: Without sizes, the browser defaults to 100vw during preloading, causing a 300px sidebar thumbnail to potentially download a 1600w desktop banner.

questions.question: What happens if an iframe element has sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin" set simultaneously when embedding untrusted content hosted on the same origin as the parent page?

options.text: The embedded script can access the parent page's DOM and remove its own sandbox attribute, completely escaping the sandbox.
The browser blocks the iframe from executing any JavaScript.
The iframe is isolated in a read-only mode where parent DOM properties are immutable.
The browser strips allow-same-origin automatically whenever allow-scripts is present.

questions.explanation: Combining allow-scripts and allow-same-origin for same-origin framed content lets the framed script traverse window.parent.document and strip the sandbox attribute, defeating sandboxing entirely.
